elements.element: The licence grant extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly includes Client's affiliates.

elements.element: The licence grant extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly includes Client's contractors acting on Client's behalf.
No perpetual duration is stated. The existence of paid-up licences is not demonstrably excluded.
No irrevocability protection is included. The existence of paid-up licences is not demonstrably excluded.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated only for breach.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no restriction limiting termination of a subscription licence to breach.

elements.element: The breach permitting termination of a subscription licence must be material.
elements.evidence: No materiality threshold for termination appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: The material breach permitting termination of a subscription licence must remain uncured.
elements.evidence: No cure right or uncured-breach condition appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: Customer may transfer the licence to any successor without the licensor's consent.
elements.evidence: The consent exception is limited to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all assets, rather than any successor.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered upon Customer's written notice to the licensor.
elements.evidence: The grant covers Client's affiliates immediately and without notice, which is broader than coverage conditioned on written notice.

elements.element: Customer may transfer the licence to a successor in an M&A transaction without the other party's consent.
elements.evidence: Section 15 dispenses with approval for assignment to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all assets.

result.reason: The redline reaches the fallback but omits all paid-up licence protections and all subscription termination protections, and its successor-transfer exception is narrower than the unqualified preferred right. It is not minimal because it also grants TrueLink a reciprocal no-consent M&A assignment right, which is unnecessary to satisfy either Customer position. The added concepts do not contradict the remaining terms, but drafting quality is reduced by the pre-existing incomplete phrase “so long as such” and by extending the assignment exception bilaterally.
